newsitem.title: JAPAN: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG LEADS SECOND TRAINING.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG LEADS SECOND TRAINING.

text.p: World Cup leader Pernilla Wiberg clocked the fastest time on Thursday in the second official training run here for two women's World Cup downhills scheduled to begin on Friday.
The 26-year-old Swede, downhill bronze medallist at the world championships less than two weeks ago in Sestriere, Italy, covered the 2,656-metre course in one minute, 37.57 seconds.
Russian Warwara Zelenskaja, who won her first World Cup downhill of the season earlier this month in Laax, Switzerland, finished .49 seconds behind.
Regine Cavagnoud of France came from 28th position to place third, 1.52 seconds behind Wiberg.
Downhill champion Hilary Lindh of the United States was seventh in 1:39.56. Silver medallist Heidi Zurbriggen of Switzerland, who has been leading the downhill rankings, was eighth in 1:39.64.
Unseasonably warm weather continued to cause problems, with training on the downhill course for next year's Nagano Winter Olympics delayed for an hour because of poor visibility.
On Wednesday, training was cancelled because of heavy rain and wet snow.
